summary: Intermittent first-token stall on chat completions following compiler routing swap
description:
Issue summary: ClaraHealth reported intermittent elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) on streaming chat completions that began after runtime compiler routing changes rolled out on 2026-03-10. Impact: ~10% of chat sessions for ClaraHealth experienced first-token stalls of 6–10s (typical TTFB is <200ms). Several sessions timed out at the client at 12s and retried, causing duplication and poor UX. Environment: production, us-west region, Dedicated pool (reserved), models impacted intermittently.

Observed behavior: Customer traces show a hard stall between request acceptance and first token emission; downstream tokens stream normally after the stall. Stalls cluster around specific sequence-length distributions (prompt+system tokens ~90–120). Not all requests are affected; sessions routed to low-latency GPU pool rarely show the issue.

Logs & captures: Customer provided SDK traces, streaming telemetry, and recorded request IDs. Support captured corresponding route IDs and GPU hostnames.

Initial hypothesis: Recent compiler routing update introduced a path that selects a quantized attention kernel for certain sequence lengths; under some path choices the KV cache warm-up triggers cross-device copies that stall first-token emission. Alternative hypothesis: routing policy inadvertently sent a subset of traffic to a heterogeneous capacity pool with different memory layout, increasing kernel selection latency for first token.

Steps to reproduce: See steps_to_reproduce field.
steps_to_reproduce: Use ClaraHealth account API key in prod (us-west dedicated pool)
Send chat completion with system prompt + user prompt leading to ~100 tokens of context
Enable streaming and log time-to-first-token using SDK trace headers
Repeat across requests to observe intermittent stalls (~1 in 10)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 09:15 - Support ingested SDK traces from customer and mapped failing request IDs to route IDs and hostnames.

2026-03-11 10:02 - SRE Priya Singh reproduced elevated TTFB in prod by replaying traffic against dedicated pool; observed stalls correlate with execution path that picks quantized attention kernel for seq_len ~128.

2026-03-11 13:40 - Engineering (Lucas Park) identified a regression in kernel_selector: an edge-case cost heuristic incorrectly favored a quantized kernel that requires an extra memory format transform on GPUs in one host-class, adding ~6s pre-token latency for first generation while KV cache warmed.

2026-03-12 02:20 - Further telemetry showed routing decision grouped ~12% of ClaraHealth traffic onto mixed-capacity nodes after routing swap; those nodes had a different CUDA/cuBLAS minor version and triggered the memory transform path more often.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Engineering reproduced the stall locally by forcing the same kernel selection and observed identical TTFB delays; subsequent profiling captured a large memcpy and kernel launch latency skew on first token only.

2026-03-12 16:30 - Regression introduced by runtime PR 4821 that adjusted kernel scoring to favor smaller working-set kernels for medium sequence lengths; PR had passed unit tests but missed this mixed-host interaction.

2026-03-13 08:00 - Temporary mitigation options evaluated: a) pin routing to low-latency pool for ClaraHealth, b) disable the new kernel heuristic in production, c) add a quick routing guard to avoid mixed-capacity nodes for streaming-first-token requests.
comments: Jordan Miles (CS) 2026-03-11: Customer reports first-token stalls causing client timeouts; provided 24 request traces and timestamps.

Priya Singh (SRE) 2026-03-11: Mapped request IDs -> hosts: several failures land on hosts gpu-mix-07 and gpu-mix-09. Reproduced locally with targeted traffic. Marking as Sev1 due to timed-out customer requests.
Lucas Park (Eng) 2026-03-12: Found kernel_selector heuristic change in PR 4821 as likely cause; preparing a minimal revert/guard. Working with SRE to scope rollback surface.
Rafael Ortega (Assignee) 2026-03-12: Applied routing guard to exclude mixed-capacity nodes for ClaraHealth's streaming routes; monitoring telemetry for TTFB improvements.
Maya Chen (Reporter) 2026-03-13: Customer confirms drop in reported stalls from ~10% -> ~1% after routing guard. Some residual failures remain; asking for ETA on proper fix.
workaround: Applied a targeted routing guard that prefers low-latency dedicated pool for ClaraHealth streaming routes; advised customer to pin to previous model variant for further stability. Workaround reduced stalls dramatically but is not a full fix.
resolution: Temporary mitigation deployed (routing guard). Engineering to land kernel_selector patch that reintroduces a safety check against memory-format-transform paths on heterogeneous hosts. Target next deploy window 2026-03-17. Postmortem and rollout checklist to be written to Confluence.
next_steps: Finish kernel_selector patch and unit/integration tests (Engineering)
Schedule canary rollout to staging and then prod (SRE/Release)
Update runtime rollout runbook with new gating checks (Docs/Eng)
Communicate timeline and mitigation to ClaraHealth CS contact
